propositions: A 0-byte enrich-drain.lock with no owner stamp created by a dead drainer process wedges enrichment forever because _acquire_advisory_lock never writes to the file and FileExistsError is not checked for staleness.
The drain lock lacks ownership metadata and staleness bounds, unlike the store write lock which has v2 owner stamps and the 1h _MKDIR_LOCK_STALE_CEILING_S ceiling.

An unstamped or aged-out drain lock must be extracted into a shared _stamp_is_stale core decision table with an asymmetric unrecognised_via_ceiling parameter so pre-existing orphans become wall-clock-ceiling-reclaimable while mkdir legacy behavior is preserved.
On FileExistsError, stamped_file_is_stale must adjudicate and permit exactly one bounded retry to reclaim and re-acquire an orphaned lock; live and recent holders are refused without mutation.
drain() must log skipped and reclaimed states at WARNING with holder description and age so wedges are visible without running doctor.
doctor's drain lock report must decode the v2 stamp and emit a real staleness verdict instead of not-assessable.
